1529664.steps:
1.) In the Firewall - Advanced Rule Options page, enable Stealth Mode.
  2.) On the remote computer, enable a packet trace utility such as Ethereal, or EtherPeek and set it to capture all traffic from the firewall in both directions.
  3.) From a remote computer, send an invalid TCP recieved out-of-state packet. Use the Nemesis tool from the command line and type nemesis tcp -v -fSA -D[WAN IP Address] This will send a SYN-ACK without first sending a SYN.
1529664.title: Firewall will not reply with RST to Invalid TCP Packets while in STEALTH Mode
1529664.description:
Original ID: 5
Original Title: Firewall will not reply with RST to Invalid TCP Packets while in STEALTH Mode
Original Description: Verify that the firewall when in stealth mode, will not send an RST reply to any source that sent an invalid TCP packet received out-of-state.
1529664.result: When Stealth Mode is enabled, the firewall will not reply with RST (reset) to invalid TCP packets received out-of-state. A message will be logged on the firewall displaying TCP packet received on non-existent/closed connection; TCP packet dropped, and list the Notes section TCP Flag(s) ACK SYN.

1529663.steps:
1.) One at a time, create a packet with the following TCP flag(s): _ - (NULL: Stealth Scan) ACK-URG FIN (FIN: Stealth Scan) FIN-PSH FIN-URG FIN-PSH-URG (XMAS: Stealth Scan) FIN-RST FIN-RDT-URG FIN-RST-PSH-URG SYN-RST SYN-FIN SYN-FIN-RST SYN-FIN-PSH SYN-FIN-RST-PSH SYN-FIN-RST-PSH-ACK SYN-FIN-RST-PSH-ACK-URG
  2.) Send the packet to the firewall.
  3.) Verify the log displays a message that the packet was dropped and contains the correct TCP flag type that was sent.
  4.) Verify that an initial connection is not established.
1529663.initial:
Either nmap, or nemesis can be used to send the packets. In the case of nemesis there is only one packet being sent and this may not be enough traffic to set off the port scan feature of the firewall. When using nemesis you may have to repeatedly send the same packet 3-6 times before you see the appropriate message.
  For nemesis type nemesis tcp -v -f[flag] -D[WAN IP Address] The following flags can be used, either singly or together: S = SYN A = ACK R = RST P = PSH F = FIN U = URG E = NULL C = NULL
  For nmap type nmap -vv --scanflags [flag] [WAN IP Address] The following flags can be used, either singly or together: SYN ACK RST PSH FIN URG NULL, use nmap -vv -sN [WAN IP Address]

1529658.steps:

  2.) Verify that the FTP Public Server wizard created the appropriate rules to allow traffic to access the server within the private network.
  3.) From a client PC on the WAN, login to the FTP Server behind the firewall.
  4.) One at a time, create a packet with the following TCP flag(s): _ - (NULL: Stealth Scan) ACK-URG FIN (FIN: Stealth Scan) FIN-PSH FIN-URG FIN-PSH-URG (XMAS: Stealth Scan) FIN-RST FIN-RDT-URG FIN-RST-PSH-URG SYN-RST SYN-FIN SYN-FIN-RST SYN-FIN-PSH SYN-FIN-RST-PSH SYN-FIN-RST-PSH-ACK SYN-FIN-RST-PSH-ACK-URG
  5.) Send the packet to the firewall.
  6.) Verify the log displays a message that the packet was dropped and contains the correct TCP flag type that was sent.
  4.) Verify that the initial connection is still established.

1529658.description:
Original ID: 1
Original Title: Invalid TCP Flags with Valid Connection Aready Established
Original Description: Verify that the firewall will drop any packets that contain invalid TCP flags, log a message containing the correct TCP flag and will keep open a connection with the device that sent the packet. This test will validate that even though a valid connection exists, and there are cached entries, an invalid packet will still be detected, dropped and logged on the firewall.
1529658.result: Firewall that receives the packet will: Continue to allow the initial connection to be opened Drop the packet Display a message in the log with the correct TCP flag(s)
